messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike detected on production inference cluster (cluster-us-west-2). p95 latency increased from 220ms -> 1.1s, p99 from 420ms -> 3.2s over the last 5m. Streaming stalls count +18%. KV eviction rate up 11k/s. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/alerts/62745

eli: ack, I'm on it. Looking at kv-metrics now.

maya: seeing customer-facing errors? any 500s or stream disconnects?

eli: brief check: 500s low (~0.2%), but streaming session drops for long generations are up. Customers using long-context models are seeing tail stalls. Noticed big increase in `kv_prefill_evictions` and slab-unused-fragments.

chao: pulling logs from the serving host group. `grep` on prefill logs shows repeated prefill->decode imbalance, lots of prefill retries and `OOM_PREFETCH` style entries. Example from host-57 snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:12Z] prefill: enqueued 48 tokens, decode backlog 310ms
[2026-03-15T09:02:12Z] eviction: slab_frag_ratio=0.78, evict_rate=11234/s
[2026-03-15T09:02:13Z] decode: worker_queue_len=22, worker_exec_ms=600
```

ops-bot: Automated mitigation candidate: reduce `prefill_concurrency` and enable `eviction_backoff` (config flag). Suggested patch: `/admin/runtime?prefill_concurrency=2&eviction_backoff=true`.

eli: trying the prefill throttle now. Running admin curl:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  https://admin.redwood/runtimes/cluster-us-west-2/config \
  -d '{"prefill_concurrency":2, "eviction_backoff":true}'
```

eli: applied. Confirmed rollout to 30% of nodes (canary). Watching p95/p99.

sam: also recommend enabling temporary slab coalescing to reduce fragmentation — that lowers eviction churn. We can toggle `slab_coalesce_window=100ms` on affected hosts.

chao: added `slab_coalesce_window=100ms` to the canary hosts. Patch command:
```
# on infra admin
adminctl set nodepool us-west-2/canary slab_coalesce_window=100ms
```

eli: after throttle+coalesce: p95 down to ~360ms, p99 down to ~1.8s, streaming stalls dropped from +18% -> +6% in 7m. Eviction rate halved.

maya: good. Any customers still impacted? I pulled top customer traces — api-key-42 had 12 stalled streams in last 10m. Support pinged them 7m ago.

sam: for safety, routing policy can fallback long-gen traffic to quantized smaller model variant (model-x-q8) to reduce memory pressure. Recommend enabling fallback for customer tier 'standard' for next 30m.

eli: enabling route fallback for long requests > 1024 tokens to model-x-q8 for 5% of traffic as a progressive rollout. curl to routes API:
```
POST /routes/fallback
{ "selector": "gen_len>1024", "fallback_model": "model-x-q8", "pct": 5 }
```

ops-bot: Route change accepted and queued for rollout.

chao: crude root cause: bursty prefill waves causing cache slab fragmentation (hot growth in small allocations), decode workers can't keep up, which then triggers aggressive evictions and paging storms. Prefill vs decode imbalance looks like prefill producers outrunning decode consumers during several incoming bursts at ~09:01-09:06.

eli: action items so far: 1) prefill throttle canary -> if stable, expand to full cluster; 2) slab coalesce enabled on canary, consider wider enable; 3) enable fallback to q8 variant for long gens; 4) increase paging throughput as a secondary mitigation.

maya: what's customer impact classification? I'd mark P2 (degraded latency, limited streaming stalls) unless support reports larger outages.

eli: agreed P2. Notifying on-call rotation and support. Logging incident in tracker: https://incidents.redwood/62745

lena: taking over in 10m. Quick notes for handoff: prefill throttle at 30% canary -> if p99 < 2s and eviction rate keeps dropping, expand to 100% in 10m. If stalls reappear, revert throttle and roll out increased decode worker pool (but that's heavier).

sam: FYI I've prepared a quick runtime patch to bump `decode_worker_limit` by +50% as fallback. Command ready: `adminctl set nodepool us-west-2 decode_worker_limit=+50%`. Hold for approval.

eli: monitoring alert configured: if p99 > 2.5s for 3 consecutive 1m buckets, auto-escalate to SRE lead and spin up paging-parallelism.

chao: logs snapshot (recent 2m) uploaded: https://logs.redwood/snapshots/62745/frag2.txt

maya: support update: emailed top-10 affected customers with short note and mitigation steps. No escalations yet.

lena: taking over now. Current state: p95=340ms, p99=1.7s, eviction_rate ~5.4k/s, streaming stalls +5%. Proceeding to expand prefill throttle to 100% over next 5m, then monitor.

eli: noted. Leaving a checklist for you in the incident doc. If anything flips back, ping pager.

lena: will do. TL;DR for handoff: root cause = prefill surge -> slab fragmentation -> eviction spiral -> paging stalls. Live mitigations = prefill throttle, slab coalesce, fallback to q8, monitoring + route control. Next: expand throttle, consider decode worker bump if needed, schedule postmortem once stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 62745 status: acknowledged -> mitigations applied -> monitoring. Escalation threshold remains p99>2.5s.

lena: closing active handoff. If stable for 30m I'll mark incident as mitigated and start a postmortem draft.
